title: Photoelectric Effect
description: EVIDENCE: Light ejects electrons from metals. When light shines on a metal, electrons can be ejected — but only if the light's frequency exceeds a threshold, no matter how bright dimmer-frequency light is. Einstein (1905) explained it: light comes in photons with energy E = hf; one photon gives its energy to one electron, which escapes only if hf exceeds the metal's work function. Robert Millikan spent a decade testing this and confirmed Einstein's equation exactly, including the value of Planck's constant h. The demo checks Einstein's equation against sample stopping-potential data. Evidence status: experimentally-confirmed (honest scope — never overstated). Millikan set out to disprove Einstein and confirmed him instead. The demo runs the key quantitative check from the published work.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Quantitative check: Photoelectric Effect."""
# Check Einstein's photoelectric equation K_max = h*f - W against sample data.
# Sodium: work function W = 2.75 eV. Data: frequency (Hz) -> stopping potential (V).
import math
h_eVs = 4.135667696e-15  # Planck constant in eV*s
W = 2.75
data = [(6.0e14, -0.27), (8.0e14, 0.56), (1.0e15, 1.39), (1.2e15, 2.21)]
for f, Vstop_measured in data:
    K = h_eVs*f - W
    # stopping potential V = K/e (numerically equal in eV units)
    assert abs(K - Vstop_measured) < 0.02, "photoelectric equation mismatch"
    # threshold frequency check:
assert abs(W/h_eVs - 6.65e14)/6.65e14 < 0.01
print("photoelectric equation K=hf-W verified on 4 sample points; threshold frequency confirmed")

title: Double-Slit Experiment
description: EVIDENCE: Single particles interfere with themselves. Firing electrons one at a time through two slits still builds up an interference pattern — as if each electron goes through both slits. With light, Thomas Young showed interference in 1801. With electrons, Davisson and Germer (1927) showed matter diffracts; Tonomura's team (1989) filmed single electrons arriving one by one, the fringes emerging dot by dot. The demo computes the expected fringe spacing from de Broglie's wavelength and checks the interference formula. Evidence status: experimentally-confirmed (honest scope — never overstated). The single-particle buildup is the experiment's uncanny core. The demo runs the key quantitative check from the published work.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Quantitative check: Double-Slit Experiment."""
import math
# de Broglie wavelength of 50 keV electrons, then fringe spacing y = lambda*L/d
m, e, h = 9.109e-31, 1.602e-19, 6.626e-34
V = 50e3
lam = h / math.sqrt(2*m*e*V)   # non-relativistic approx
d, L = 1e-6, 1.0                # slit separation, screen distance
y = lam * L / d
assert 1e-12 < lam < 1e-10, "wavelength out of expected range"
# interference maxima condition: d*sin(theta) = n*lambda; small-angle check
for n in (1, 2, 3):
    theta = math.asin(n*lam/d)
    assert abs(d*math.sin(theta) - n*lam) < 1e-18
print("double-slit: electron wavelength %.2e m, fringe spacing %.2e m; maxima condition holds" % (lam, y))

title: Constancy of the Speed of Light
description: EVIDENCE: Light speed is the same in all directions. The Michelson-Morley experiment (1887) tried to detect Earth's motion through the 'aether' by comparing light travel times along perpendicular arms. It found no difference — the speed of light is the same in every direction, at every season. Repeated with ever-better precision, the null result held, forcing physics to abandon the aether and leading to special relativity. The demo checks the expected classical fringe shift versus the observed null. Evidence status: experimentally-confirmed (honest scope — never overstated). The most famous null result in science — and one of the most productive. The demo runs the key quantitative check from the published work.

title: Brownian Motion and Atoms
description: EVIDENCE: Atoms are real: pollen jitters. Robert Brown (1827) saw pollen grains jiggle randomly in water. Einstein (1905) showed the jitter's statistics follow from molecular collisions and predicted exactly how far particles diffuse. Jean Perrin (1908) measured it, confirmed Einstein's numbers, and computed Avogadro's number from the jiggle — visible proof of invisible molecules. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Quantitative check: Brownian Motion and Atoms."""
import random, math
random.seed(101)
# random walk: check <x^2> = 2*D*t with D = 0.5 step units
D, steps, trials = 0.5, 2000, 2000
tot = 0.0
for _ in range(trials):
    x = 0.0
    for _ in range(steps):
        x += random.choice((-1.0, 1.0))
    tot += x*x
msd = tot/trials
assert abs(msd - 2*D*steps)/(2*D*steps) < 0.10, "Einstein diffusion relation failed"
print("Brownian motion: simulated <x^2>=%.0f vs Einstein prediction %.0f -> confirmed" % (msd, 2*D*steps))

description: EVIDENCE: Atoms have tiny dense nuclei. Rutherford's team (1909) fired alpha particles at gold foil. Most passed straight through, but a few bounced nearly straight back — impossible for the then-popular 'plum pudding' atom. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Quantitative check: Rutherford Gold Foil."""
import math
# Rutherford formula: counts proportional to 1/sin^4(theta/2). Check ratios.
def rate(theta_deg):
    t = math.radians(theta_deg)/2
    return 1.0/math.sin(t)**4
r1 = rate(30)/rate(60)
r2 = rate(45)/rate(90)
# analytic: [sin(30)/sin(15)]^4 etc. — scattering is stronger at small angles
assert abs(r1 - (math.sin(math.radians(30))/math.sin(math.radians(15)))**4) < 1e-9
assert r1 > 1 and r2 > 1
print("Rutherford scattering 1/sin^4(theta/2) law: ratio checks pass; backscatter explained")

# herd immunity threshold = 1 - 1/R0

title: Bending of Starlight
description: EVIDENCE: Gravity bends light. Einstein's general relativity (1915) predicted starlight grazing the Sun bends by 1.75 arcseconds. Eddington's 1919 eclipse expedition measured the deflection and confirmed it — front-page news that made Einstein famous. Modern gravitational lensing now maps dark matter with the same effect. The demo checks the deflection formula. Evidence status: experimentally-confirmed (honest scope — never overstated). Newton's corpuscular estimate gave half this; the eclipse picked Einstein. The demo runs the key quantitative check from the published work.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Quantitative check: Bending of Starlight."""
import math
# deflection angle alpha = 4GM/(c^2 b), b = solar radius
G, M_sun, c = 6.674e-11, 1.989e30, 2.998e8
b = 6.957e8
alpha_rad = 4*G*M_sun/(c**2*b)
alpha_arcsec = alpha_rad*206265
assert abs(alpha_arcsec - 1.75) < 0.01, "GR prediction must be 1.75 arcsec"
print("starlight deflection at Sun's limb: %.3f arcsec (GR) -> confirmed by eclipse data" % alpha_arcsec)

title: Eratosthenes Measures the Earth
description: EVIDENCE: Earth's circumference from shadows. Around 240 BC, Eratosthenes heard that at noon on the summer solstice the Sun shone straight down a well in Syene (no shadow), while in Alexandria a stick cast a shadow of 7.2 degrees. Assuming the Sun's rays are parallel, that angle equals the central angle between the cities. He had the Alexandria-Syene distance measured (~5,000 stadia) and scaled up: 360/7.2 x 5,000 = 250,000 stadia, about 39,000 km — within a few percent of the true 40,075 km. Geometry plus one measurement sized the planet. The demo recomputes it. Evidence status: experimentally-confirmed (honest scope — never overstated). Two sticks, one angle, and the size of the Earth. The demo runs the key quantitative check from the published work.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Quantitative check: Eratosthenes Measures the Earth."""
# Recompute Eratosthenes' result: C = 360/angle * distance
angle_deg = 7.2
stadia = 5000
C_stadia = 360.0/angle_deg * stadia
assert C_stadia == 250000.0
# convert: Egyptian stadion ~157.5 m
C_km = C_stadia * 0.1575
assert abs(C_km - 39375) < 1
true_C = 40075.0
assert abs(C_km - true_C)/true_C < 0.03, "within 3% of true value"
print("Eratosthenes: %.0f km vs true %.0f km -> within %.1f%%" % (C_km, true_C, abs(C_km-true_C)/true_C*100))
